outcome: pelvic floor dysfunction (including pelvic organ prolapse, colorectal-anal dysfunction, urinary distress)
cohort: 32 postpartum mothers aged 18 to 45 years old who had undergone cesarean delivery.
finding: Diastasis rectus abdominis (DRA) was found to be a strong predictor of pelvic floor dysfunction, including prolapse, colorectal-anal dysfunction, and urinary distress, but no correlation was found with sacroiliac joint dysfunction or health-related quality of life.
cross-section timing: during the postpartum period (exact timing not specified)
